note: The browser WITH its sandbox, run by a normal user, as on any Linux that allows user namespaces. Same seed, same bytes: the engine published as firefox-68 against the candidate, on one machine, with the same core and wrapper, after the control: the published engine against ITSELF (the A/A; a difference is a broken control, exit 2, and the A/B is not run). On a pull request (no candidate: INVPW_BINARY_PATH is the published engine, no INVISIBLE_SEAL_FILE) the A/A is the whole test, on the first two seeds of the candidate set (all five when the pull request changes a file of this oracle: the step of e2e.yml that runs scripts/ci_ab_pr_seeds.py exports AB_ORACLE_PR_SEEDS), and saves both dumps and the diff under $AB_ORACLE_OUT or $RUNNER_TEMP/invpw-evidence/ab-oracle. scripts/ci_ab_oracle.py runs the host gate's dump (scripts/ci_host_gate.py dump: the persona seeds of ci/persona-seeds.json, each at its own DPR with nothing pinned, the whole page of scripts/host_gate; the `candidate` set of 5 seeds that reach every webgl renderer and every DPR, or with AB_ORACLE_SEED_SET=final and AB_ORACLE_SHARD=i/n the 20 seeds that reach every value of every dimension split over n jobs) twice, once with the firefox-68 binary (the release's seal.json, then the core's own download.ensure_binary under that seal: the archive's sha256 is checked against the seal) and once with the candidate binary of the leg under its own seal, and compares every leaf of every visit: the only differences allowed are the `noise` entries of scripts/host_gate/exceptions.json and the diag. keys; anything else is red with the leaf, the two values and the seed; fewer leaves than the host gate's reference holds (16439 per visit; a DPR the reference does not record is held to the least of those it does) is red. The files (dump-68.json, dump-68-again.json, diff-a-a.json and, with a candidate, dump-candidate.json and diff.json) are the artifact ab-oracle-<os> of the leg. 1 = the one test; the comparator's own cases (51, the A/A's among them) are in tests/test_ab_oracle.py, the persona seeds' (15) in tests/test_persona_cover.py, in the rows of the whole unit suite. Needs the engine's binary (INVPW_BINARY_PATH) and, for the A/B, the candidate's seal (INVISIBLE_SEAL_FILE) and the network (the release assets of firefox-68). The engine of the candidate must accept the core of the leg and the 68 engine must accept it too: a core that declares something the published engine refuses is a red of this suite, not of the engine.

Network A/B oracle: the P4 journey, HTTPS h1/h2 (ClientHello, h2 frames, header order), HTTP/3 (transport parameters, H3 SETTINGS), WebRTC through the coherent SOCKS5 lab gateway, DNS through the fake DoH, and an idle launch; transcripts compared leaf by leaf, direct connections red on either side. A/A first (the published engine twice: a difference is a broken control; ci/ab-network-volatile.json holds the leaves the A/A proved volatile, and may only shrink), then the published engine against the candidate. Without a candidate (a PR's e2e) the A/A alone, on the first seed (all five when the pull request changes a file of this oracle: AB_NETWORK_PR_SEEDS), in jobs of its own in e2e.yml on Linux and on Windows (the shared e2e jobs leave this file out).

Host A/B oracle: the whole TRACE of a closed run, from the launch to the exit of the browser, after the same journey. Compared: the processes by kind (the parent, -contentproc type, sandboxingKind, isForBrowser, the helpers by what they ran) with their count, except for the kinds of type tab whose count follows the idle time (only their presence counts), and the host paths the tree touched, judged by one rule (red if and only if a path is in all the measured launches of one engine and in no launch of the other, the long launches included; every other path that differs is listed in not-judged.json, not judged); what is ours (the package, the profile and temp dirs of the launch, the run cache, its own shared memory) leaves the comparison as a class. Linux: strace of the whole tree. Windows: the process-creation audit (event 4688, with the command line) and an ETW file trace of Kernel-File, which need an administrator. It has jobs of its own in e2e.yml on Linux and on Windows (a measurement shares the machine with no other browser), and its footprints keep the lifecycle of the tree (who started and ended when, how) and how the close ended. Each engine run starts with a discarded warm-up launch whose trace is kept and listed apart (what only the warm-up did, with the process that did it); only the tree of the launch is compared (a Windows service's paths are counted by process name and left out), and a path or a kind that differs names the processes to blame. A/A first, then the published engine against the candidate; the one declared difference (Linux glxtest, gone on the 69) is in ci/ab-host-expected.json, applied by kind, a list that may only shrink. There is no list of noise. Without a candidate (a PR e2e) the A/A alone, on the first two seeds (all five when the pull request changes a file of this oracle: AB_HOST_PR_SEEDS).

linux_only: A signal sent to the parent of the browser with os.kill, the core the kernel writes and gdb reads, and the signal line of strace exist on Linux only: Windows has no counterpart of this test. What a Windows launch that did not end with 0 leaves (the `.extra` files and the minidump names, read from the crash folders) is held by the unit tests of the recorder with fake launches, and by every Windows leg of the three oracles, which are red on any parent that does not end with 0.
note: The recorder of the host oracle, tested on a launch that dies on purpose: scripts/ci_ab_host.py crash-probe launches the engine once under the oracle's stand-in (strace of the tree, cores enabled, a crash watcher), sends SIGSEGV to the browser's parent with os.kill and closes it as the oracle closes its launches; the test passes when the oracle reports RED (exit 1, `FAIL the parent process exited with code ...: seed N, launch crash`) and the artifact (RUNNER_TEMP/invpw-evidence/ab-host-crash) holds the signal line of the strace log (strace-signals.txt, strace-tail.txt), the core run through gdb (gdb-core.*.txt: `thread apply all bt`, the MOZ_CRASH reason, `info sharedlibrary`), the build ids and what the collectors did not find (said.txt). It fails when the oracle says green for a launch that died, when the evidence is missing and when the probe did not run; the red of the probe does not make the job red. It runs in the job of the host oracle on Linux (e2e-host: strace, gdb and elfutils installed, kernel.core_pattern pointed at INVPW_CORE_DIR), after the A/A, and is left out of the shared e2e job (OWN_JOB_FILES).
